pages.title: Welcome to Amharic
paragraphs: Amharic is one of the main languages of Ethiopia and the country's federal working language. Tens of millions of people speak it, in Ethiopia and in communities around the world.
It's a Semitic language, related to Arabic and Hebrew. You'll be learning the standard Amharic of Addis Ababa.

pages.title: A script of its own
paragraphs: Amharic is written in the fidel. Each character is a consonant and a vowel together, so the fidel comes in families: one base shape for each consonant, changed a little for each of seven vowels.
There are 34 families, 238 characters in all — but learn the seven vowel marks once and they work across every family. The fidel reads left to right and has no capital letters.

pages.title: Sounds to listen for
paragraphs: Most Amharic sounds will feel familiar. A few are new: popped sounds made with a closed throat, and consonants held a little longer, which can change what a word means.
Every letter and word comes with a recording to copy. At first the sounds are also written in Latin letters to help you; as you get comfortable, you can hide them and read the fidel itself.

pages.title: How the course works
paragraphs: In six weeks of short daily lessons — about 15 to 20 minutes each — you'll learn the whole fidel, along with your first words, greetings and short stories.
Each lesson starts with a quick review, then you listen, look, write and say. Mistakes are part of learning: anything you miss comes back at the end of the lesson and in later reviews.
Your progress is saved in this browser on this device. Headphones and a microphone help, but you don't need them.
